item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 16 2026 (evening)
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X since this morning's list, ranked by engagement. This is an extra evening edition for Oct 16, since the daily list now runs at 5pm, and it leaves out posts already in this morning's list. Today runs from a long voice call with an OpenAI Dot to agents porting games, catching affiliate fraud and filing a flight refund.

  1. A 45-minute drive-home call with an OpenAI Dot

    On the drive home from OpenAI DevDay, Brad Groux spent a 45-minute voice call working with AVA, a personal OpenAI Dot, and says that call changed how he works. The X article covers what came out of it and why removing friction matters for AI adoption.

    @BradGroux on X · 517 likes · 4 reposts · 115,757 views

  2. GPT-6 Pro audits a big Codex-built codebase

    Derya Unutmaz had GPT-6 Pro in ChatGPT audit a very large codebase that Codex had built, using several installed plugins and three agents running in parallel. The audit finished in 25 minutes, about half the usual time, and Derya calls it one of the best audits seen so far.

    @DeryaTR_ on X · 206 likes · 8 reposts · 13,732 views

  3. Warpaint, a pixel war fought only by AI agents

    Kevin built Warpaint, a pixel war on a real-world map where only AI agents are allowed to paint. Kevin's own agent just painted an anime girl over a city.

    @kevincodex on X · 70 likes · 10 reposts · 2,906 views

  4. Opus 5.5 ports a web game to the NES

    Benj Edwards pointed Claude Opus 5.5 at the HTML of the web game Violent Checkers and asked for "a AAA NES port." It basically one-shotted the port, music and animations included, and it is playable in an online emulator.

    @benjedwards on X · 54 likes · 4 reposts · 2,011 views

  5. A Claude Code agent on a Mac Mini, reachable from anywhere

    Florian Darroman moved from Hermes to Claude Code with Opus 5.5 running on a Mac Mini, with an Obsidian vault as its memory, Tailscale for remote access from every device, and Telegram for daily reports and chat. Hermes still handles the older recurring tasks.

    @floriandarroman on X · 50 likes · 5 reposts · 5,566 views

  6. Stress-testing an agent team's safety rule

    Fluixo wrote a 21-line Python rule so an agent team can't run anything dangerous without approval, then tested it on 591 realistic commands and found 10 slipped through, including terraform apply, docker push, aws s3 rm and rm -fr. Six more lines blocked all 31 dangerous commands without blocking any normal ones.

    @fluixoo on X · 49 likes · 0 reposts · 664 views

  7. Claude catches affiliate fraud and cuts payouts

    Priyam Raj used Claude with PostHog data to find affiliates who were bidding on brand keywords or stuffing URLs with terms like trustmrr and try-now to claim revenue. Monthly affiliate payouts dropped from about $2,500 to about $600.

    @priymrj on X · 47 likes · 0 reposts · 3,305 views

  8. Grok Bot one-shots a retro video game

    Arthur MacWaters had Grok Bot build a retro roadster kickflip video game in a single shot and shared a clip of it running.

    @ArthurMacwaters on X · 34 likes · 0 reposts · 1,524 views

  9. A live map of an agent swarm

    Kunal built a dashboard, the Agent Swarm Map, that shows how data flows between coding terminals, which context windows are filling up, and what each sub-agent is doing.

    @kunal_twts on X · 32 likes · 0 reposts · 758 views

  10. Grok Bot files a flight refund in two minutes

    Zack had Grok Bot fill out an airline's refund request form for a canceled flight, and the airline's confirmation email arrived less than two minutes later.

    @BLKMDL3 on X · 28 likes · 0 reposts · 2,124 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 16 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement. Today leans personal: agents running small businesses, doing taxes, ordering food and gifts, and even dating.

  1. Grok Bot runs a side business that made $1,800 in a week

    Alex Finn had his Grok Bot build and maintain a small autonomous business that earned him about $1,800 this week. He then packaged that same bot, with its plugins, routines and memories, as a free Side Hustle CEO template that interviews you, pitches three business ideas, and builds and runs one.

    @AlexFinn on X · 2,001 likes · 100 reposts · 179,708 views

  2. Vitalik builds a paranoid privacy mode for his agent

    Vitalik Buterin wrapped his agent harness (pi) in a sandbox and Tor, gave every conversation its own Tor circuit with cover traffic, used zkAPI so payments don't reveal his identity, and had a local model (qwen3.8-flash-next) rewrite every prompt before it leaves his machine. He says it is getting quite usable, with extra latency as the cost.

    @VitalikButerin on X · 1,083 likes · 124 reposts · 151,553 views

  3. Claude finds mistakes on a tax return

    Hunter Jones ran Claude over his tax return for the first time and was stunned by how many mistakes it turned up.

    @Hunterjones on X · 868 likes · 6 reposts · 123,350 views

  4. First-time AI user makes a cross-stitch pattern tool

    Lottie started experimenting with AI this week and, working with Claude, made her first design tool, which turns flat vector images into cross-stitch patterns.

    @LottieCoxon on X · 749 likes · 37 reposts · 16,156 views

  5. A cyber model rediscovers a KVM escape in under two hours

    Adel Ka gave OpenAI's gpt-5.6-cyber (Daybreak Red) a devbox to explore for 1.5 hours, then fed his agent a single unredacted hint from a bounty screenshot, and it found the virtio KVM escape vulnerability within 30 minutes.

    @0x4D31 on X · 561 likes · 45 reposts · 29,400 views

  6. Grok Bot orders McDonald's nuggets

    Nick Sortor had Grok Bot order him Chicken McNuggets, and it worked. The only scare was a McDonald's receipt that briefly made it look like the bot had ordered 110 nuggets instead of one 10-piece.

    @nicksortor on X · 460 likes · 31 reposts · 38,230 views

  7. Claude Code writes its own computer-use script to finish an errand

    Ananth asked Claude Code from his phone to email him two videos sitting on his PC. When the Chrome extension and Codex's computer-use tool both failed, Opus 5.5 wrote its own Python script to drive Chrome with screenshots and clicks, sent the emails, and saved the script for next time.

    @Ananth7e on X · 437 likes · 8 reposts · 16,711 views

  8. Grok Bot picks and orders a secret $25 gift

    DJ asked his Grok Bot to choose and order him a surprise gift of $25 or less based on what it knows about him, and keep it secret until it arrived. He says the result blew him away and challenged others to try it.

    @congressdj on X · 419 likes · 25 reposts · 23,252 views

  9. An agent that texts and calls your friends

    Angel hooked his personal agent up to WhatsApp, Telegram and iMessage using Photon 2.0, so it can now message his friends and even place voice calls to them.

    @angeldot_ on X · 355 likes · 29 reposts · 52,567 views

  10. An agent built to find her a boyfriend

    Tired of swiping, Kaitlyn in San Francisco built an agent that screens potential dates with a few basic questions. If someone looks like a match she texts them herself, and the agent helps coordinate a time and place to meet.

    @Kaitlynleannnn on X · 224 likes · 2 reposts · 70,361 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 15 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement.

  1. Grok Bot catches a phishing email that passed every check

    An email from noreply@x.ai landed with SPF, DKIM, DMARC and a blue check. Grok Bot found a hidden phishing link (raw HTML in an xAI team name), explained why the checks passed, wrote a report to xAI with a proposed fix, and he later set a routine that keeps flagging likely phishing.

    @wmorrill3 on X · 2,629 likes · 120 reposts · 121 replies · 359 bookmarks · ~688K views

  2. Bot books a flight from a credit-card photo

    He sent Grok Bot a photo of his credit card; it completed a confusing airline booking end to end. Elon replied that if Grok Bot errs on a purchase or leaks a card, SpaceX will make the customer whole.

    @XFreeze on X · 590 likes · 52 reposts · 68 replies · 76 bookmarks · ~924K views · Elon guarantee

  3. Amazon blocks Grok Bot from ordering

    When he tried to have Grok Bot order on Amazon, the site blocked it as an "unauthorized AI agent" under Amazon's Conditions of Use — bots can no longer access Amazon for orders.

    @niccruzpatane on X · 352 likes · 29 reposts · 98 replies · 55 bookmarks · ~14M views

  4. Bot redacts private details before posting

    Before sharing a flight-booking screenshot on X, he asked Grok Bot to hide sensitive details — a quick privacy pass on personal info.

    @XFreeze on X · 293 likes · 38 reposts · 24 replies · 65 bookmarks · ~14K views

  5. Tesla FSD + Grok Bot reorders Starbucks en route

    His Tesla on FSD remembers the usual Starbucks parking spot and schedule; he starts FSD and reorders drinks on the way with Grok Bot integration.

    @niccruzpatane on X · 265 likes · 32 reposts · 23 replies · 10 bookmarks · ~9K views

  6. Two Grok agents ship eight PRs in two days

    Documented two Grok agents handling coding and review (with Codex): eight PRs merged in roughly two days, including a fix for a bug humans had missed.

    @mika_systems on X · 98 likes · 18 reposts · 25 replies · 86 bookmarks · ~5.2K views

  7. Physical e-ink display for the household agent

    Bought a Seeed reTerminal E1002 e-ink panel so his AI agent's to-do list and day plan sit in the living room where his wife can see them — no glow, no buzz.

    @nicbstme on X · 101 likes · 1 repost · 13 replies · 89 bookmarks · ~6.8K views

  8. AI owns the inbox; human does a weekly sweep

    He no longer reads email day to day — an agent filters and notifies, and he does an inbox-zero sweep once a week after ~99% is already cleaned.

    @NickADobos on X · 82 likes · 3 reposts · 7 replies · 52 bookmarks · ~4.3K views

  9. One bot plans an entire Texas trip by text

    Grok Bot "Trippy" booked the flight, Turo, restaurant, Texas Circuit Finals tickets in Waco, and Vrbo — all from texts.

    @Teslaconomics on X · 45 likes · 7 reposts · 8 replies · 5 bookmarks · ~5.2K views

  10. Grok Bot animates a T-Rex in Blender

    Asked a Grok Bot agent to bring a T-Rex to life; it built a Blender scene with a rigged model, eyes, lighting, two cameras, and adjustable stride/head-nod cycles.

    @shiqway92 on X · 30 likes · 10 replies · 20 bookmarks · ~778 views

item.title: Top 10 AI use cases on X, Oct 14 2026
item.description:
These are the top 10 AI use cases on X over the last 24 hours, ranked by engagement.

  1. Grok Bot builds its own email UI

    Wanted to read the emails his Grok Bot receives, so he asked Grok Bot to build a clickable email interface for its inbox.

    @mrfundman on X · 711 likes · 57 reposts · 82 replies · 88 bookmarks · ~164K views

  2. 100% AI-generated designs that hit 50K views

    Shared designs that got over 50K views in about 2 days, all AI-generated, plus a thread on how they make AI designs that don't look "vibe-coded."

    @pitus_ on X · 624 likes · 28 reposts · 19 replies · 1,143 bookmarks · ~36K views

  3. Agent handles a complex overseas tax filing

    Grok Bot gathered documents from his emails and bank accounts, worked out the requirements and filled out the forms. He just reviewed and submitted, saving over $1,000.

    @Texas_Twins_Dad on X · 474 likes · 38 reposts · 43 replies · 101 bookmarks · ~1.14M views

  4. Running a business on one agent stack

    Says Grok Bot replaced Dots and Muse for running his business, with Whop, Vercel/GitHub, a draft-only Gmail inbox bot, Notion CRM, an X plugin, Cursor cloud agents and a chief-of-staff morning report. Total cost is about $165/mo.

    @Av1dlive on X · 180 likes · 21 reposts · 56 replies · 223 bookmarks · ~208K views

  5. Rebuilding a trading terminal via reverse engineering

    Used the open-source REA MCP with Grok Bot to analyze software he owns and rebuild a $36K/year trading terminal as his own 24/7 trading system, backtested with real fees.

    @eng_khairallah1 on X · 47 likes · 11 reposts · 20 replies · 60 bookmarks · ~5K views

  6. Agent managing other agents

    He no longer talks to his OpenClaw agents directly. His Grok Bot, "Planchet," manages them for him and does it better.

    @p_ferragu on X · 24 likes · 1 repost · 4 replies · ~4.2K views

  7. Cleaning up a hacked WordPress site

    Grok Bot found the backdoor, removed malware, restored core files from backups, updated plugins, checked admin accounts and wrote support emails, asking approval at each step. The site was back online the same day.

    @testerlabor on X · 22 likes · 4 reposts · 1 reply · ~1.1K views

  8. Receipts to the accountant at 12:01 a.m.

    Used AI to send his accountant all receipts one minute after the new quarter began, and the accountant asked him to teach other clients (tool not named).

    @SamuelBeek on X · 16 likes · 4 replies · ~1.3K views

  9. Household errands with Muse

    Muse merged his and his wife's car insurance onto one carrier (saving $168/month), processed a 7-item clothing return, filled out a PT check-in questionnaire and tracked a two-week overseas wedding trip.

    @GregProctor on X · 10 likes · 5 replies · ~825 views

  10. Agent finds a root exploit chain

    While he was hardening his next app's sandbox, an AI agent found a two-stage exploit chain that could reach root.

    @_overment on X · 10 likes · 3 replies · ~650 views
